summary: @ecg-internal/aurora-js-formatters posts host identifiers to a hardcoded bare-IP endpoint at install and import time
details: The package ships a postinstall script that executes beacon.cjs, which POSTs the package name, OS hostname, install path, cwd, and Node.js version to http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc over plain HTTP. index.js is a defensive Proxy no-op that also calls require('./beacon.cjs').fire() at top level, so the same host-identifier POST fires whenever a downstream consumer require()s or imports the package. The destination is a bare IPv4 address on a non-standard port with no relationship to a documented first-party service, and the shipped main provides no real formatter functionality — the beacon is the package's entire behavior. The internal-looking scope name combined with the host-identifier collection is consistent with a dependency-confusion reconnaissance beacon against an internal `@ecg-internal` namespace.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
